title: A homogeneous mono-unstable polyhedron with fourteen vertices
publication_date: Set to the actual date of first public release.
description:
We present an explicit convex polyhedron with fourteen vertices whose uniformly distributed volume has exactly one unstable equilibrium with respect to its center of mass. The vertices have small integer coordinates; the polyhedron has thirty-six edges and twenty-four triangular facets, with exactly two stable, one saddle and one unstable equilibrium.

The construction varies the thickness along a double-spiral outline to control the projected volume centroid without adding an apex. A self-contained exact proof establishes the equilibrium counts. A further certificate proves that every vertical contraction by a factor 0 < t <= 1 preserves the face lattice and the unique unstable equilibrium.

This deposit contains the preprint, LaTeX and Markdown sources, exact coordinates, three verification programs, complete equilibrium reports, figure source, integrity hashes and an execution transcript. The command "python reproduce.py" verifies the results using only the Python standard library.

The result is a constructive upper bound of fourteen vertices, not a proof of minimality. The paper explicitly discusses the earlier public sixteen-vertex construction. The full equilibrium count (2,1,1) is asserted for the supplied example, while the contraction family is certified only for the unique unstable equilibrium.

The work was developed with substantial assistance from Claude (Anthropic) and Codex (OpenAI), under the author's direction. It is a preprint; no external human expert review is claimed.
